newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Eng shares up on garbage incinerator order.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Eng shares up on garbage incinerator order.

text.p: Shares in Mitsui Engineering & Shipbuilding Co Ltd surged on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on Wednesday morning on news that the company is expected to win an order for a garbage incinerator plant, dealers said.
The shares were up 30 yen at 252 yen as of 0125 GMT, their highest level since the beginning of the year. Mitsui was the top percentage gainer on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
The company was also the most heavily traded issue.
The company said on Wednesday that it expects to win a contract to build a next-generation garbage incinerator plant from a group of local governments in western Japan.
The new plant, which will have a disposal capacity of 220 tonnes per day, is expected to be in operation in around 2001, a company spokesman said.
The spokesman declined to say the amount of the contract, but pointed out that, in general, a garbage incinerator of that size would cost around 14 billion yen.
The volume of dioxin emissions from the new plant would meet government guildelines which set the allowed dioxin emission at less than 0.1 nanogram per one cubic metre.
Dioxin is a highly toxic by-product of some industrial processes and is known to cause a wide range of diseases, including cancer.
